verses.344: Ah, land of buzzing insects, beyond the rivers of Ethiopia,
verses.345: Sending ambassadors by sea, in papyrus boats on the waters! Go, swift messengers, to a nation tall and bronzed, To a people dreaded near and far, a nation strong and conquering, whose land is washed by rivers.
verses.346: All you who inhabit the world, who dwell on earth, When the signal is raised on the mountain, look! When the trumpet blows, listen!
verses.347: For thus says the LORD to me: I will quietly look on from where I dwell, Like the glowing heat of sunshine, like a cloud of dew at harvest time.
verses.348: Before the vintage, when the flowering is ended, and the blooms are succeeded by ripening grapes, Then comes the cutting of branches with pruning hooks and the discarding of the lopped-off shoots.
verses.349: They shall all be left to the mountain birds of prey, and to the beasts in the land; The birds of prey shall summer on them and on them all the beasts of the earth shall winter.
verses.350: Then will gifts be brought to the LORD of hosts from a people tall and bronzed, from a people dreaded near and far, a nation strong and conquering, whose land is washed by rivers - to Mount Zion where dwells the name of the LORD of hosts. [1-2] Papyrus boats: light and serviceable vessels made of bundles of papyrus stalks and sealed with pitch. Egypt, ruled by a dynasty from Ethiopia, had invited Judah to join a coalition against Assyria, but Isaiah bade the ambassadors return to their own people. Land of buzzing insects: the region of the Upper Nile where these multiplied with great rapidity. Previous - Next Copyright © Libreria Editrice Vaticana
verses.351: Oracle on Egypt: See, the LORD is riding on a swift cloud on his way to Egypt; The idols of Egypt tremble before him, the hearts of the Egyptians melt within them.
verses.352: I will rouse Egypt against Egypt: brother will war against brother, Neighbor against neighbor, city against city, kingdom against kindgom.
verses.353: The courage of the Egyptians ebbs away within them, and I will bring to nought their counsel; They shall consult idols and charmers, ghosts and spirits.
verses.354: I will deliver Egypt into the power of a cruel master, A harsh king who shall rule over them, says the Lord, the LORD of hosts.
verses.355: The waters shall be drained from the sea, the river shall shrivel and dry up;
verses.356: Its streams shall become foul, and the canals of Egypt shall dwindle and dry up. Reeds and rushes shall wither away,
verses.357: and bulrushes on the bank of the Nile; All the sown land along the Nile shall dry up and blow away, and be no more.
verses.358: The fishermen shall mourn and lament, all who cast hook in the Nile; Those who spread their nets in the water shall pine away.
verses.359: The linen-workers shall be disappointed, the combers and weavers shall turn pale;
verses.360: The spinners shall be crushed, all the hired laborers shall be despondent.
verses.361: Utter fools are the princes of Zoan! the wisest of Pharaoh's advisers give stupid counsel. How can you say to Pharaoh, "I am a disciple of wise men, of ancient kings"?
verses.362: Where then are your wise men? Let them tell you and make known What the LORD of hosts has planned against Egypt.
verses.363: The princes of Zoan have become fools, the princes of Memphis have been deceived. The chiefs of her tribes have led Egypt astray.
verses.364: The LORD has prepared among them a spirit of dizziness, And they have made Egypt stagger in whatever she does, as a drunkard staggers in his vomit.
verses.365: Egypt shall have no work to do for head or tail, palm branch or reed.
verses.366: On that day the Egyptians shall be like women, trembling with fear, because of the LORD of hosts shaking his fist at them.
verses.367: And the land of Judah shall be a terror to the Egyptians. Every time they remember Judah, they shall stand in dread because of the plan which the LORD of hosts has in mind for them.
verses.368: On that day there shall be five cities in the land of Egypt speaking the language of Canaan and swearing by the LORD of hosts; one shall be called "City of the Sun."
verses.369: On that day there shall be an altar to the LORD in the land of Egypt, and a sacred pillar to the LORD near the boundary.
verses.370: It shall be a sign and a witness to the LORD of hosts in the land of Egypt, when they cry out to the LORD against their oppressors, and he sends them a savior to defend and deliver them.
verses.371: The LORD shall make himself known to Egypt, and the Egyptians shall know the LORD in that day; they shall offer sacrifices and oblations, and fulfill the vows they make to the LORD.
verses.372: Although the LORD shall smite Egypt severely, he shall heal them; they shall turn to the LORD and he shall be won over and heal them.
verses.373: On that day there shall be a highway from Egypt to Assyria; the Assyrians shall enter Egypt, and the Egyptians enter Assyria, and Egypt shall serve Assyria.
verses.374: On that day Israel shall be a third party with Egypt and Assyria, a blessing in the midst of the land,
verses.375: when the LORD of hosts blesses it: "Blessed be my people Egypt, and the work of my hands Assyria, and my inheritance, Israel." Cruel master: the king of Assyria. [11,13] Zoan, later known as Tanis, and Memphis (in Hebrew, Noph) were the key cities of the Nile Delta. Head or tail, palm branch or reed: the leaders or the people; cf ⇒ Isaiah 9:13, ⇒ 14. Five cities: colonies of Jews living together and speaking their languages, Hebrew and Aramaic; cf Jer 43. City of the Sun: the meaning is uncertain, but the reference seems to be to the city known later as Heliopolis. Previous - Next Copyright © Libreria Editrice Vaticana
verses.376: In the year the general sent by Sargon, king of Assyria, fought against Ashdod and captured it,
verses.377: the LORD gave a warning through Isaiah, the son of Amoz: Go and take off the sackcloth from your waist, and remove the sandals from your feet. This he did, walking naked and barefoot.
verses.378: Then the LORD said: Just as my servant Isaiah has gone naked and barefoot for three years as a sign and portent against Egypt and Ethiopia,
verses.379: so shall the king of Assyria lead away captives from Egypt, and exiles from Ethiopia, young and old, naked and barefoot, with buttocks uncovered (the shame of Egypt).
verses.380: They shall be dismayed and ashamed because of Ethiopia, their hope, and because of Egypt, their boast.
verses.381: The inhabitants of this coastland shall say on that day, "Look at our hope! We have fled here for help and deliverance from the king of Assyria; where can we flee now?" [2-6] The symbolic act of the prophet conveyed the idea that Assyria would lead captive the Egyptians and Ethiopians. The Judeans and their allies would then realize the folly of having trusted in them. Previous - Next Copyright © Libreria Editrice Vaticana
verses.382: Oracle on the wastelands by the sea: Like whirlwinds sweeping in waves through the Negeb, there comes from the desert, from the fearful land,
verses.383: A cruel sight, revealed to me: the traitor betrays, the despoiler spoils. "Go up, Elam; besiege, O Media; I will put an end to all groaning!"
verses.384: Therefore my loins are filled with anguish, pangs have seized me like those of a woman in labor; I am too bewildered to hear, too dismayed to look.
verses.385: My mind reels, shuddering assails me; My yearning for twilight has turned into dread.
verses.386: They set the table, spread out the rugs; they eat, they drink. Rise up, O princes, oil the shield!
verses.387: For thus says my Lord to me: Go, station a watchman, let him tell what he sees.
verses.388: If he sees a chariot, a pair of horses, Someone riding an ass, someone riding a camel, Then let him pay heed, very close heed.
verses.389: Then the watchman cried, "On the watchtower, O my Lord, I stand constantly by day; And I stay at my post through all the watches of the night.
verses.390: Here he comes now: a single chariot, a pair of horses; He calls out and says, 'Fallen, fallen is Babylon, And all the images of her gods are smashed to the ground.'"
verses.391: O my people who have been threshed, beaten on my threshing floor! What I have heard from the LORD of hosts, The God of Israel, I have announced to you.
verses.392: Oracle on Edom: They call to me from Seir, "Watchman, how much longer the night? Watchman, how much longer the night?"
verses.393: The watchman replies, "Morning has come, and again night. If you will ask, ask; come back again."
verses.394: Oracle on Arabia: In the thicket in the nomad country spend the night, O caravans of Dedanites.
verses.395: Meet the thirsty, bring them water; you who dwell in the land of Tema, greet the fugitives with bread.
verses.396: They flee from the sword, from the whetted sword; From the taut bow, from the fury of battle.
verses.397: For thus says the Lord to me: In another year, like those of a hireling, all the glory of Kedar shall come to an end.
verses.398: Few of Kedar's stalwart archers shall remain, for the LORD, the God of Israel, has spoken. Wastelands by the sea: Babylonia. Negeb: the desert south of Judah. Elam . . . Media: nations which, under the leadership of Cyrus, captured Babylon in 538 B.C. End to all groaning: those who were captive of Babylon shall be freed. Babylon is destroyed while its leaders are feasting; cf Daniel 5. Oil the shield: shields were oiled and greased so as to divert blows more easily. [11-12] Seir: another name for Edom. The Edomites ask the prophet how much longer they must suffer (the night of suffering); he answers ambiguously: "Liberation (morning) and further suffering (night)," but perhaps they will later receive a more encouraging answer (ask, come back again). [13-14] Arabia: that is, the nomad country. Dedanites: an Arab tribe associated with Edom and Tema, and living east of the Red Sea; cf ⇒ Genesis 10:7; ⇒ 25:3; ⇒ Jeremiah 25:23. Year . . . of a hireling: see note on ⇒ 16:14. Kedar: a nomad tribe in Arabia; cf ⇒ Isaiah 42:11; ⇒ 60:7; ⇒ Psalm 120:5. Previous - Next Copyright © Libreria Editrice Vaticana
verses.399: Oracle of the Valley of Vision: What is the matter with you now, that you have gone up, all of you, to the housetops,
verses.400: O city full of noise and chaos, O wanton town! Your slain are not slain with the sword, nor killed in battle.
verses.401: All your leaders fled away together, fled afar off; All who were in you were captured together, captured without the use of a bow.
verses.402: At this I say: Turn away from me, let me weep bitterly; Do not try to comfort me for the ruin of the daughter of my people.
verses.403: It is a day of panic, rout and confusion, from the Lord, the GOD of hosts, in the Valley of Vision. Walls crash; they cry for help to the mountains.
verses.404: Elam takes up the quivers, Aram mounts the horses, and Kir uncovers the shields.
verses.405: Your choice valleys are filled with chariots, and horses are posted at the gates,
verses.406: and shelter over Judah is removed. On that day you looked to the weapons in the House of the Forest;
verses.407: you saw that the breaches in the City of David were many; you collected the water of the lower pool.
verses.408: You numbered the houses of Jerusalem, tearing some down to strengthen the wall;
verses.409: you made a reservoir between the two walls for the water of the old pool. But you did not look to the city's Maker, nor did you consider him who built it long ago.
verses.410: On that day the Lord, the GOD of hosts, called on you To weep and mourn, to shave your head and put on sackcloth.
verses.411: But look! you feast and celebrate, you slaughter oxen and butcher sheep, You eat meat and drink wine: "Eat and drink, for tomorrow we die!"
verses.412: This reaches the ears of the LORD of hosts - You shall not be pardoned this wickedness till you die, says the Lord, the GOD of hosts.
verses.413: Thus says the Lord, the GOD of hosts: Up, go to that official, Shebna, master of the palace,
verses.414: Who has hewn for himself a sepulcher on a height and carved his tomb in the rock: "What are you doing here, and what people have you here, that here you have hewn for yourself a tomb?"
verses.415: The LORD shall hurl you down headlong, mortal man! He shall grip you firmly
verses.416: And roll you up and toss you like a ball into an open land To perish there, you and the chariots you glory in, you disgrace to your master's house!
verses.417: I will thrust you from your office and pull you down from your station.
verses.418: On that day I will summon my servant Eliakim, son of Hilkiah;
verses.419: I will clothe him with your robe, and gird him with your sash, and give over to him your authority. He shall be a father to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and to the house of Judah.
verses.420: I will place the key of the House of David on his shoulder; when he opens, no one shall shut, when he shuts, no one shall open.
verses.421: I will fix him like a peg in a sure spot, to be a place of honor for his family;
verses.422: On him shall hang all the glory of his family: descendants and offspring, all the little dishes, from bowls to jugs.
verses.423: On that day, says the LORD of hosts, the peg fixed in a sure spot shall give way, break off and fall, and the weight that hung on it shall be done away with; for the LORD has spoken. [1-8] Valley of Vision: while the people live in revelry and disorder, the prophet foresees the impending doom of the city. Elam, Aram, Kir: all allies of Assyria. Kir: perhaps the same people referred to in ⇒ Amos 1:5. [8-11] Defense measures, in which the inhabitants of Jerusalem placed their trust instead of relying on God. House of the Forest: an armory built by Solomon; its columns of wood suggested the trees of a forest; cf ⇒ 1 Kings 7:2; ⇒ 10:17. Shebna: referred to as the scribe in ⇒ Isaiah 36:3. Eliakim: also referred to in ⇒ Isaiah 36:3; he is described as loyal to God. Key: symbol of authority; cf ⇒ Matthew 16:19; ⇒ Rev 3:7. [24-25] If Eliakim should anger God, he and his family (compared here to dishes, bowls and jugs) will suffer disaster. Previous - Next Copyright © Libreria Editrice Vaticana
verses.424: Oracle on Tyre: Wail, O ships of Tarshish, for your port is destroyed; From the land of the Kittim 2 the news reaches them.
verses.425: Silence! you who dwell on the coast, you merchants of Sidon, Whose messengers crossed the sea
verses.426: over the deep waters. The grain of Shihor, the harvest of the Nile, was her revenue, and she the merchant among nations.
verses.427: Shame, O Sidon, fortress on the sea, for the sea has spoken: "I have not been in labor, nor given birth, nor raised young men, nor reared virgins."
verses.428: When it is heard in Egypt they shall be in anguish at the news of Tyre.
verses.429: Pass over to Tarshish, wailing, you who dwell on the coast!
verses.430: Is this your wanton city, whose origin is from old, Whose feet have taken her to dwell in distant lands?
verses.431: Who has planned such a thing against Tyre, the bestower of crowns, Whose merchants are princes, whose traders are the earth's honored men?
verses.432: The LORD of hosts has planned it, to disgrace all pride of majesty, to degrade all the earth's honored men.
verses.433: Cross to your own land, O ship of Tarshish; the harbor is no more.
verses.434: His hand he stretches out over the sea, he shakes kingdoms; The LORD has ordered the destruction of Canaan's strongholds.
verses.435: You shall exult no more, he says, you who are now oppressed, virgin daughter Sidon. Arise, pass over to the Kittim, even there you shall find no rest.
verses.436: (This people is the land of the Chaldeans, not Assyria.) She whom the impious founded, setting up towers for her, Has had her castles destroyed, and has been turned into a ruin.
verses.437: Lament, O ships of Tarshish, for your haven is destroyed.
verses.438: On that day, Tyre shall be forgotten for seventy years. With the days of another king, at the end of seventy years, it shall be for Tyre as in the song about the harlot:
verses.439: Take a harp, go about the city, O forgotten harlot; Pluck the strings skillfully, sing many songs, that they may remember you.
verses.440: At the end of the seventy years the LORD shall visit Tyre. She shall return to her hire and deal with all the world's kingdoms on the face of the earth.
verses.441: But her merchandise and her hire shall be sacred to the LORD. It shall not be stored up or laid away, but from her merchandise those who dwell before the LORD shall eat their fill and clothe themselves in choice attire. [1-4,12-14] These verses refer to Sidon, ⇒ Isaiah 23:5-11 to Tyre. Kittim: Cyprus. Shihor: a synonym for the Nile. The sea: brings to distant coasts the news that Sidon must disown her children; her people are dispersed. Canaan's strongholds: the fortresses of Phoenicia. The gloss here identifies she whom the impious founded with the land of the Chaldeans. Seventy years: a conventional period of time indicating simply a long disaster; cf ⇒ Jeremiah 25:11; ⇒ 29:10. Describes the conversion of Tyre. Previous - Next Copyright © Libreria Editrice Vaticana
verses.442: Lo, the LORD empties the land and lays it waste; he turns it upside down, scattering its inhabitants:
verses.443: Layman and priest alike, servant and master, The maid as her mistress, the buyer as the seller, The lender as the borrower, the creditor as the debtor.
verses.444: The earth is utterly laid waste, utterly stripped, for the LORD has decreed this thing.
verses.445: The earth mourns and fades, the world languishes and fades; both heaven and earth languish.
verses.446: The earth is polluted because of its inhabitants, who have transgressed laws, violated statutes, broken the ancient covenant.
verses.447: Therefore a curse devours the earth, and its inhabitants pay for their guilt; Therefore they who dwell on earth turn pale, and few men are left.
verses.448: The wine mourns, the vine languishes, all the merry-hearted groan.
verses.449: Stilled are the cheerful timbrels, ended the shouts of the jubilant, stilled is the cheerful harp.
verses.450: They cannot sing and drink wine; strong drink is bitter to those who partake of it.
verses.451: Broken down is the city of chaos, shut against entry, every house.
verses.452: In the streets they cry out for lack of wine; all joy has disappeared and cheer has left the land.
verses.453: In the city nothing remains but ruin; its gates are battered and desolate.
verses.454: Thus it is within the land, and among the peoples, As with an olive tree after it is beaten, as with a gleaning when the vintage is done.
verses.455: These lift up their voice in acclaim; from the sea they proclaim the majesty of the LORD:
verses.456: "For this, in the coastlands, give glory to the LORD! In the coastlands of the sea, to the name of the LORD, the God of Israel!"
verses.457: From the end of the earth we hear songs: "Splendor to the Just One!" But I said, "I am wasted, wasted away. Woe is me! The traitors betray: with treachery have the traitors betrayed!
verses.458: Terror, pit, and trap are upon you, inhabitant of the earth;
verses.459: He who flees at the sound of terror will fall into the pit; He who climbs out of the pit will be caught in the trap. For the windows on high will be opened and the foundations of the earth will shake.
verses.460: The earth will burst asunder, the earth will be shaken apart, the earth will be convulsed.
verses.461: The earth will reel like a drunkard, and it will sway like a hut; Its rebellion will weigh it down, until it falls, never to rise again."
verses.462: On that day the LORD will punish the host of the heavens in the heavens, and the kings of the earth on the earth.
verses.463: They will be gathered together like prisoners into a pit; They will be shut up in a dungeon, and after many days they will be punished.
verses.464: Then the moon will blush and the sun grow pale, For the LORD of hosts will reign on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, glorious in the sight of his elders.
verses.465: O LORD, you are my God, I will extol you and praise your name; For you have fulfilled your wonderful plans of old, faithful and true.
verses.466: For you have made the city a heap, the fortified city a ruin; The castle of the insolent is a city no more, nor ever to be rebuilt.
verses.467: Therefore a strong people will honor you, fierce nations will fear you.
verses.468: For you are a refuge to the poor, a refuge to the needy in distress; Shelter from the rain, shade from the heat. As with the cold rain,
verses.469: as with the desert heat, even so you quell the uproar of the wanton.
verses.470: On this mountain the LORD of hosts will provide for all peoples A feast of rich food and choice wines, juicy, rich food and pure, choice wines.
verses.471: On this mountain he will destroy the veil that veils all peoples, The web that is woven over all nations;
verses.472: he will destroy death forever. The Lord GOD will wipe away the tears from all faces; The reproach of his people he will remove from the whole earth; for the LORD has spoken.
verses.473: On that day it will be said: "Behold our God, to whom we looked to save us! This is the LORD for whom we looked; let us rejoice and be glad that he has saved us!"
verses.474: For the hand of the LORD will rest on this mountain, but Moab will be trodden down as a straw is trodden down in the mire.
verses.475: He will stretch forth his hands in Moab as a swimmer extends his hands to swim; He will bring low their pride as his hands sweep over them.
verses.476: The high-walled fortress he will raze, and strike it down level with the earth, with the very dust. [1-8] Victory in messianic times. This mountain: Zion, symbol of the heavenly Jerusalem. Moab: symbol of God's enemies. Previous - Next Copyright © Libreria Editrice Vaticana
verses.477: On that day they will sing this song in the land of Judah: "A strong city have we; he sets up walls and ramparts to protect us.
verses.478: Open up the gates to let in a nation that is just, one that keeps faith.
verses.479: A nation of firm purpose you keep in peace; in peace, for its trust in you."
verses.480: Trust in the LORD forever! For the LORD is an eternal Rock.
verses.481: He humbles those in high places, and the lofty city he brings down; He tumbles it to the ground, levels it with the dust.
verses.482: It is trampled underfoot by the needy, by the footsteps of the poor.
verses.483: The way of the just is smooth; the path of the just you make level.
verses.484: Yes, for your way and your judgments, O LORD, we look to you; Your name and your title are the desire of our souls.
verses.485: My soul yearns for you in the night, yes, my spirit within me keeps vigil for you; When your judgment dawns upon the earth, the world's inhabitants learn justice.
verses.486: The wicked man, spared, does not learn justice; in an upright land he acts perversely, and sees not the majesty of the LORD.
verses.487: O LORD, your hand is uplifted, but they behold it not; Let them be shamed when they see your zeal for your people: let the fire prepared for your enemies consume them.
verses.488: O LORD, you mete out peace to us, for it is you who have accomplished all we have done.
verses.489: O LORD, our God, other lords than you have ruled us; it is from you only that we can call upon your name.
verses.490: Dead they are, they have no life, shades that cannot rise; For you have punished and destroyed them, and wiped out all memory of them.
verses.491: You have increased the nation, O LORD, increased the nation to your own glory, and extended far all the borders of the land.
verses.492: O LORD, oppressed by your punishment, we cried out in anguish under your chastising.
verses.493: As a woman about to give birth writhes and cries out in her pains, so were we in your presence, O LORD.
verses.494: We conceived and writhed in pain, giving birth to wind; Salvation we have not achieved for the earth, the inhabitants of the world cannot bring it forth.
verses.495: But your dead shall live, their corpses shall rise; awake and sing, you who lie in the dust. For your dew is a dew of light, and the land of shades gives birth.
verses.496: Go, my people, enter your chambers, and close your doors behind you; Hide yourselves for a brief moment, until the wrath is past.
verses.497: See, the LORD goes forth from his place, to punish the wickedness of the earth's inhabitants; The earth will reveal the blood upon her, and no longer conceal her slain. This verse refers to the restoration of Israel in messianic times under the figure of the resurrection of the dead; cf Ezekial 37. Previous - Next Copyright © Libreria Editrice Vaticana
verses.498: On that day, The LORD will punish with his sword that is cruel, great, and strong, Leviathan the fleeing serpent, Leviathan the coiled serpent; and he will slay the dragon that is in the sea.
verses.499: On that day - The pleasant vineyard, sing about it!
verses.500: I, the LORD, am its keeper, I water it every moment; Lest anyone harm it, night and day I guard it.
verses.501: I am not angry, but if I were to find briers and thorns, In battle I should march against them; I should burn them all.
verses.505: Expunging and expelling, I should strive against them, carrying them off with my cruel wind in time of storm.
verses.506: This, then, shall be the expiation of Jacob's guilt, this the whole fruit of the removal of his sin: He shall pulverize all the stones of the altars like pieces of chalk; no sacred poles or incense altars shall stand.
verses.507: For the fortified city shall be desolate, an abandoned pasture, a forsaken wilderness, where calves shall browse and lie. Its boughs shall be destroyed,
verses.508: its branches shall wither and be broken off, and women shall come to build a fire with them. This is not an understanding people; therefore their maker shall not spare them, nor shall he who formed them have mercy on them.
verses.509: On that day, The LORD shall beat out the grain between the Euphrates and the Wadi of Egypt, and you shall be gleaned one by one, O sons of Israel.
verses.510: On that day, A great trumpet shall blow, and the lost in the land of Assyria and the outcasts in the land of Egypt Shall come and worship the LORD on the holy mountain, in Jerusalem. Leviathan . . . dragon: symbols of the forces of evil which God vanquishes even as he overcame primeval chaos; cf notes on ⇒ Job 3:8; ⇒ 7:12. God's people will not be treated as sternly as were their enemies. [8-9] Israel will make peace with God and destroy all signs of idolatrous worship. [10-11] The fortified city: symbol of the powers of evil; see note on ⇒ Isaiah 24:10. The Euphrates and the Wadi of Egypt: the ideal borders of Israel; cf ⇒ Genesis 15:18; ⇒ 2 Kings 24:7. The triumph of God's people is described in eschatological language; they will gather in Jerusalem from Assyria and Egypt. Previous - Next Copyright © Libreria Editrice Vaticana
verses.511: Woe to the majestic garland of the drunkard Ephraim, To the fading blooms of his glorious beauty, on the head of him who is stupefied with wine.
verses.512: Behold, the LORD has a strong one and a mighty, who, like a downpour of hail, a destructive storm, Like a flood of water, great and overflowing, levels to the ground with violence;
verses.513: With feet that will trample the majestic garland of the drunkard Ephraim.
verses.514: The fading blooms of his glorious beauty on the head of the fertile valley Will be like an early fig before summer: when a man sees it, he picks and swallows it at once.
verses.515: On that day the LORD of hosts will be a glorious crown And a brilliant diadem to the remnant of his people,
verses.516: A spirit of justice to him who sits in judgment, And strength to those who turn back the battle at the gate.
verses.517: But these also stagger from wine and stumble from strong drink: Priest and prophet stagger from strong drink, overpowered by wine; Led astray by strong drink, staggering in their visions, tottering when giving judgment.
verses.518: Yes, all the tables are covered with filthy vomit, with no place left clean.
verses.519: "To whom would he impart knowledge? To whom would he convey the message? To those just weaned from milk, those taken from the breast?
verses.520: For he says, 'Command on command, command on command, rule on rule, rule on rule, here a little, there a little!'"
verses.521: Yes, with stammering lips and in a strange language he will speak to this people
verses.522: to whom he said: This is the resting place, give rest to the weary; Here is repose - but they would not listen.
verses.523: So for them the word of the LORD shall be: "Command on command, command on command, Rule on rule, rule on rule, here a little, there a little!" So that when they walk, they stumble backward, broken, ensnared, and captured.
verses.524: Therefore, hear the word of the LORD, you arrogant, who rule this people in Jerusalem:
verses.525: Because you say, "We have made a covenant with death, and with the nether world we have made a pact; When the overwhelming scourge passes, it will not reach us; For we have made lies our refuge, and in falsehood we have found a hiding place," -
verses.526: Therefore, thus says the Lord GOD: See, I am laying a stone in Zion, a stone that has been tested, A precious cornerstone as a sure foundation; he who puts his faith in it shall not be shaken.
verses.527: I will make of right a measuring line, of justice a level. - Hail shall sweep away the refuge of lies, and waters shall flood the hiding place.
verses.528: Your covenant with death shall be canceled and your pact with the nether world shall not stand. When the overwhelming scourge passes, you shall be trampled down by it.
verses.529: Whenever it passes, it shall take you; morning after morning it shall pass, By day and by night; terror alone shall convey the message.
verses.530: For the bed shall be too short to stretch out in, and the cover too narrow to wrap in.
verses.531: For the LORD shall rise up as on Mount Perazim, bestir himself as in the Valley of Gibeon, To carry out his work, his singular work, to perform his deed, his strange deed.
verses.532: Now, be arrogant no more lest your bonds be tightened, For I have heard from the Lord, the GOD of hosts, the destruction decreed for the whole earth.
verses.533: Give ear and hear my voice, pay attention and listen to what I say:
verses.534: Is the plowman forever plowing, always loosening and harrowing his land for planting?
verses.535: When he has leveled the surface, does he not scatter gith and sow cumin, Put in wheat and barley, with spelt as its border?
verses.536: He has learned this rule, instructed by his God.
verses.537: Gith is not threshed with a sledge, nor does a cartwheel roll over cumin. But gith is beaten out with a staff, and cumin crushed for food with a rod.
verses.538: No, he does not thresh it unendingly, nor does he crush it with his noisy cartwheels and horses.
verses.539: This too comes from the LORD of hosts; wonderful is his counsel and great his wisdom. Ephraim: the northern kingdom. Its capital, Samaria, was built upon a hill, suggestive of a majestic garland adorning the head of the drunken kingdom. A strong one and a mighty: Assyria. [9-10] The words of those who ridicule Isaiah. The Hebrew of ⇒ Isaiah 28:10 by its very sound, conveys the idea of mocking imitation of what the prophet says, as though he spoke like a stammering child: SAU LASAU, SAU LASAU, CAU LACAU, CAU LACAU, ZE'ER SHAM, ZE'ER SHAM. But in v 13 God repeats these words in deadly earnest, putting them in the mouth of the victorious pagan army. God will answer the mockers and defend Isaiah. Strange language: spoken by the invading army. [15,18] A covenant with death, and with the nether world: an alliance with foreign powers, such as Egypt and Babylon, to prevent death and destruction. Have made lies . . . a hiding place: this confidence in human aid proves to be false and deceitful, incapable of averting the dreaded disaster. Overwhelming scourge: the flood of the Assyrian invasion; cf ⇒ Isaiah 8:7-8. A stone in Zion: the true and sure foundation of salvation promised by God to the Davidic dynasty (cf ⇒ Isaiah 7:13-16; ⇒ 9:1-6), which the Apostles saw fulfilled in Christ the universal Savior; cf ⇒ 1 Peter 2:6-8; ⇒ Romans 9:33; ⇒ 10:9-11. Cornerstone: the assurance of salvation rejected by Israel in the prophet's time, is reflected by the psalmist ( ⇒ Psalm 118:22) and fulfilled in the Person of Christ; cf ⇒ Matthew 21:42; ⇒ Luke 20:17; ⇒ Acts 4:11; ⇒ Romans 9:33; ⇒ 1 Peter 2:7. Mount Perazim . . . Valley of Gibeon: where David defeated the Philistines; cf ⇒ 2 Sam 5:20, ⇒ 25; ⇒ 1 Chron 14:11, ⇒ 16. [23-29] The practical variation of the farmer's work taught him by God reflects God's dealing with his people, wisely adapted to circumstances; he does not crush their weakness altogether; cf Isaiah 29. Gith . . . cumin: herbs used in seasoning food. Spelt: a variety of wheat. Previous - Next Copyright © Libreria Editrice Vaticana
verses.540: Woe to Ariel, Ariel, the city where David encamped! Add year to year, let the feasts come round.
verses.541: But I will bring distress upon Ariel, with mourning and grief. You shall be to me like Ariel,
verses.542: I will encamp like David against you; I will encircle you with outposts and set up siege works against you.
verses.543: Prostrate you shall speak from the earth, and from the base dust your words shall come. Your voice shall be like a ghost's from the earth, and your words like chirping from the dust.
verses.544: The horde of your arrogant shall be like fine dust, the horde of the tyrants like flying chaff. Then suddenly, in an instant,
verses.545: you shall be visited by the LORD of hosts, With thunder, earthquake, and great noise, whirlwind, storm, and the flame of consuming fire.
verses.546: Then like a dream, a vision in the night, Shall be the horde of all the nations who war against Ariel with all the earthworks of her besiegers.
verses.547: As when a hungry man dreams he is eating and awakens with an empty stomach, Or when a thirsty man dreams he is drinking and awakens faint and dry, So shall the horde of all the nations be, who make war against Zion.
verses.548: Be irresolute, stupefied; blind yourselves and stay blind! Be drunk, but not from wine, stagger, but not from strong drink!
verses.549: For the LORD has poured out on you a spirit of deep sleep. He has shut your eyes (the prophets) and covered your heads (the seers).
verses.550: For you the revelation of all this has become like the words of a sealed scroll. When it is handed to one who can read, with the request, "Read this," he replies, "I cannot; it is sealed."
verses.551: When it is handed to one who cannot read, with the request, "Read this," he replies, "I cannot read."
verses.552: The Lord said: Since this people draws near with words only and honors me with their lips alone, though their hearts are far from me, And their reverence for me has become routine observance of the precepts of men,
verses.553: Therefore I will again deal with this people in surprising and wondrous fashion: The wisdom of its wise men shall perish and the understanding of its prudent men be hid.
verses.554: Woe to those who would hide their plans too deep for the LORD! Who work in the dark, saying, "Who sees us, or who knows us?"
verses.555: Your perversity is as though the potter were taken to be the clay: As though what is made should say of its maker, "He made me not!" Or the vessel should say of the potter, "He does not understand."
verses.556: But a very little while, and Lebanon shall be changed into an orchard, and the orchard be regarded as a forest!
verses.557: On that day the deaf shall hear the words of a book; And out of gloom and darkness, the eyes of the blind shall see.
verses.558: The lowly will ever find joy in the LORD, and the poor rejoice in the Holy One of Israel.
verses.559: For the tyrant will be no more and the arrogant will have gone; All who are alert to do evil will be cut off,
verses.560: those whose mere word condemns a man, Who ensnare his defender at the gate, and leave the just man with an empty claim.
verses.561: Therefore thus says the LORD, the God of the house of Jacob, who redeemed Abraham: Now Jacob shall have nothing to be ashamed of, nor shall his face grow pale.
verses.562: When his children see the work of my hands in his midst, They shall keep my name holy; they shall reverence the Holy One of Jacob, and be in awe of the God of Israel.
verses.563: Those who err in spirit shall acquire understanding, and those who find fault shall receive instruction. [1-2] Ariel: variously interpreted to mean "lion of God" or "hearth (altar) of God," a poetic name for Jerusalem; or perhaps to be read as Uru-el, "foundation of God," an archaic name for the Jebusite city of Jerusalem; like that Ariel, against which David encamped, it will be besieged by God. verses.736: When he was worshiping in the temple of his god Nisroch, his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer slew him with the sword and fled into the land of Ararat. His son Esarhaddon reigned in his stead. A proverbial expression. In the Bible the pangs of childbirth often typify extreme anguish; cf ⇒ Isaiah 13:8; ⇒ Jeremiah 6:24; ⇒ Micah 4:9, ⇒ 10. In this instance there is reference to the desperate situation of Hezekiah from which he was scarcely able to free himself. Tirhakah: may have been general of the Egyptian army in 701 B.C.; later he became king, one of the Ethiopian dynasty of Egyptian kings (c. 690-664 B.C.). Many consider that this account in Isaiah combines features of two originally distinct sieges of Jerusalem by Sennacherib. In contrast to the empty boasting of the Assyrians, Hezekiah proclaims the Lord as God over all the kingdoms of the earth. You: Hezekiah. A sign: it is difficult to know the nature of this sign. Either it is merely a proverbial expression to signify that prosperity follows adversity, or it indicates that after two years the normal conditions of life will be resumed. The destruction of Sennacherib's army is also recorded by Herodotus, a Greek historian of the fifth century B.C. It was probably due to the bubonic plague, but the sacred author attributes it to its ultimate cause, God through his angel. The violent death of Sennacherib (681 B.C.) is also mentioned in non-biblical sources. It occurred twenty years after his invasion of Judea. Previous - Next Copyright © Libreria Editrice Vaticana

verses.932: In the LORD shall be the vindication and the glory of all the descendants of Israel." Anointed: in Hebrew, meshiah, from which the word "Messiah" is derived; from its Greek translation Christos, we have the name "Christ." Applied to kings, "anointed" originally referred only to those of Israel, but it is here given to Cyrus because he is the agent of the Lord. Bronze doors: of Babylon. The Gentiles will come to know the true God; cf also ⇒ 45:20-25. Create woe: God permits evil for the sake of a greater good. The Vulgate rendering gives a more precise messianic sense to this verse, using "just one" and "savior" in place of justice and salvation. The Advent liturgy uses the Vulgate form, Rorate coeli desuper . . ., to express the world's longing for the coming of Christ. No one may challenge God's freedom of action, exemplified here by the selection of Cyrus as his anointed. One: Cyrus, called by God for the deliverance and restoration of Israel. Egypt . . . Ethiopia . . . Sabeans: the Egyptians and their allies who, when conquered by Cyrus, are seen as acknowledging the God of Israel to be the one true God; cf ⇒ 43:3. God is hidden: he dwells invisibly in the holy of holies. Waste: an allusion to the beginning of creation, when the earth was waste and void ( ⇒ Genesis 1:2), the same Hebrew word, tohu, being used in both passages. Responding to the people's complaint of utter abandonment by God, the prophet shows that their sins were responsible for their banishment. Since there was no bill of divorce, the bond between the Lord and his people still exists and he will ultimately save them. Israel's faith in God is weak; she does not answer his call, nor believe in his promises of deliverance.
